facts: Problem: Phase 0.1 requires creating a monorepo structure and installing tooling for the multi-agent orchestration platform. Current state is asset-only (agents, contracts, lib); no project structure exists. Decisions needed on monorepo strategy, package manager, build tools, and dev infrastructure.

Success criteria: npm workspaces configured and initialized, all dependencies installed, TypeScript compiles in root and both workspaces, npm run dev starts frontend (port 5173) and backend (port 3000) without errors, ESLint and Prettier configured, all files pass linting.

Constraints: Node.js v24.13.1 is installed (meets >18 requirement). Existing lib/*.js files must be preserved (to be refactored in later phases, not deleted). ASSET_MIGRATION_STATUS.md designates lib/ refactoring for Phase 1, 2, 3 (config-loader, run-tracker, api-server). Monorepo must follow final directory layout from ROADMAP.md (frontend/, backend/, shared/, data/, docs/). Must use npm workspaces (no Yarn, Lerna, or pnpm for consistency with existing npm 10.8.2).

Option A: npm workspaces with root-level configuration (Recommended). Pros: Native npm feature, zero additional dependencies, all workspace scripts run from root, shared node_modules optimization, simple CI/CD, works with npm 8+. Cons: Less mature than Yarn/Lerna, fewer plugins/tooling. When to choose: When simplicity and native npm support is priority (recommended for MVP).

Option B: Yarn workspaces (Alternative). Pros: Mature, performance optimized, plugina plugin ecosystem. Cons: Requires yarn install (breaking change from npm), dependency on external tool, increases complexity. When to choose: Only if npm workspaces prove insufficient or for advanced monorepo tooling.

Option C: Lerna (Legacy Alternative). Pros: Extensive monorepo history, good for publishing. Cons: Overkill for this use case, heavyweight, poor recent maintenance, deprecated in favor of nx. When to choose: Not recommended; consider only if cross-package publishing needed post-Phase 28.

Key decisions needed: (1) npm workspaces vs. alternatives? Answer: npm workspaces (native, no external dependency). (2) Vite + React 18 or alternatives for frontend? Answer: Vite (fast HMR, explicit TypeScript, shadows framework choice). React 18 (hooks, concurrent features, wide adoption). (3) Express + TypeScript or alternatives for backend? Answer: Express (lightweight, well-understood, existing lib/api-server.js port target). TypeScript (type safety, dev experience). (4) Shared types in shared/ workspace or distributed? Answer: shared/ workspace with shared/types/ subdirectory for unified type definitions. (5) Build toolchain (Webpack, esbuild, etc.)? Answer: Vite (frontend, out-of-box), TypeScript tsc + ts-node (backend, simple). (6) Test runners? Answer: Vitest (frontend, Vite-native), Jest (backend, standard). (7) Linting/formatting? Answer: ESLint + Prettier (standard combo, no Biome to avoid fragmentation).

Dependencies/tools to install: Root (npm workspaces): typescript@latest, eslint, prettier, tsconfig. Frontend: react@18, react-dom@18, react-router-dom@6, vite@latest, @vitejs/plugin-react, tailwindcss, postcss, autoprefixer, shadcn/ui, vitest, @testing-library/react. Backend: express, typescript, ts-node, ts-node-dev, jest, @types/express, @types/node. All: prettier, eslint, @typescript-eslint/parser, @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin. Skip: babel (Vite handles transpilation), Webpack (Vite is simpler), Lerna (npm workspaces sufficient), Socket.io (Phase 22 for real-time monitoring).

Acceptance tests (high level): (1) Root package.json has workspaces array with frontend, backend, shared. (2) npm install succeeds from root without errors. (3) frontend/package.json exists with React, Vite, TypeScript deps. (4) backend/package.json exists with Express, TypeScript deps. (5) shared/package.json exists (minimal or stub). (6) All tsconfig.json files parse and strict mode enabled. (7) npm run lint runs ESLint across workspaces. (8) npm run build compiles frontend (dist/) and backend (dist/). (9) npm run dev starts Vite dev server on 5173 + Express on 3000. (10) New backend/src/server.ts exists and imports express. (11) New frontend/src/App.tsx exists as React component. (12) .eslintrc.json and .prettierrc.json exist at root. (13) .env.example exists with placeholder vars for both frontend and backend.

risks: Risk: npm workspaces not fully compatible with all tools (e.g., old ESLint plugins, custom monorepo tooling) | Impact: Build or CI failures | Mitigation: Test ESLint, Jest, TypeScript in monorepo mode early; use --workspaces flag in commands
Risk: Vite HMR issues in Windows or remote dev environments | Impact: Hot reload fails, dev loop broken | Mitigation: Configure HMR polling in vite.config.ts if needed; test on target platform early

Risk: TypeScript strict mode creates immediate compilation errors in lib/ refactor targets | Impact: Setup blocked by legacy code | Mitigation: Use separate tsconfig for lib/ with strict=false during Phase 1; tighten in Phase 2+ refactoring
Risk: Port 3000 or 5173 already in use on developer machine | Impact: Dev server fails to start | Mitigation: Document how to change ports in .env.example; script to find available ports

Risk: ESLint/Prettier conflicts with existing code style (e.g., lib/ has different convention) | Impact: Lint errors block setup | Mitigation: Add lib/ to eslintignore during Phase 1; lint only frontend/backend; enforce in Phase 2+

Risk: Circular dependencies between shared/, frontend/, and backend/ in monorepo | Impact: Build or module resolution failures | Mitigation: Use clear layering (shared has no dependencies on frontend/backend; backend can use shared; frontend can use shared)

Risk: npm install with workspaces takes excessive time or disk space | Impact: Setup takes >30 min, discourages local development | Mitigation: Use npm ci instead of npm install in CI; local caching; document expected setup time (5–10 min typical)

Risk: Git ignores not set correctly; lib/ or node_modules accidentally committed | Impact: Repository bloat, future sync issues | Mitigation: Configure .gitignore early; use git check-ignore to validate

Risk: Shared workspace (shared/package.json) not initialized or lacks required exports | Impact: Frontend/backend import errors | Mitigation: Create minimal shared/package.json stub in Phase 1; populate in Phase 2 when data models defined

Risk: TypeScript version mismatch between workspaces causes compile errors | Impact: Some workspaces work, others fail | Mitigation: Specify single TypeScript version in root package.json; all workspaces inherit via npm workspaces hoisting
